horses.spotlight_comment: 5f For 3yo+ (70 = 10st) Minimum weight 8-7 Penalties (after calculation of the handicap) 7lb extra for each race won Weight for age 3 from 4yo+ 10lb Penalty value 1st £€7,068 2nd £€2,268 3rd £€1,068 4th £€468 5th £€228 6th £€108 GD-YLD Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR Poweracclaim 4 10-3h J Murtagh Yudish Geerdharry (7) 10-1 73 63 75 Has posted some fine runs in defeat in maidens over 6f-7f including here last time; has early speed so could cope with the drop in trip with the hood worn last time retained; considered. Sporting Hero 6 9-13b W Durkan Jamie Orr (7) 7-1 69 58 76 Nine AW wins but is a maiden on turf after 18 runs; however, he ran a cracker on soft ground at Bellewstown last time and this drying surface should suit better; a squeak. Arctic Steps 4 9-12p R O'Sullivan Reese Holohan (7) 6-1 68 59 74 AW winner over this trip in November and fine efforts in defeat back there last twice, including when just behind Sporting Hero; has won on turf so has a shout. Asdana 4 9-11v W McCreery Sam Coen (2) 5-1 67 48 77 Won over this trip at Cork last August and some fine efforts in defeat since including a fourth at Bellewstown last time; back to her winning mark so considered; can be slowly away. Nouvel Espoir 6 9-9 J Barcoe E E Ryan (7) 16-1 65 65 75 Three wins including over C&D; well beaten in soft ground on Curragh return but this surface will suit better; inexperienced rider. Edmond Halley 4 9-7p K Cotter Joseph Harnett (7) 20-1 63 62 75 Best efforts came in 5f-6f maidens at this track last October on yld/sft ground; well below that level in three handicaps including on the AW last time; this track does suit; cheekpieces back on. Verified 5 9-7 G Keane Emily Grifferty (7) 12-1 63 60 75 Maiden after 19 starts for former yard but several fine efforts in defeat including here; ground-versatile and could run well if ready enough on return. Verhoyen 11 9-6p M Grassick Sadhbh Tormey (7) 25-1 62 69 72 Fine servant is a seven-time turf winner though didn't score in 2025; has run well in defeat at this track but has never won over 5f; poor last time; opposed. Irish Ballet 4 9-5t H De Bromhead Conor Cusack (7) 20-1 61 - 72 Best run came when third in a C&D maiden as a 2yo; however, she has been well below that since including three AW runs back from an absence; opposed. Kilmood Susan 4 9-4 M Mulvany Shay Wallace (7) 25-1 60 65 71 Won a Cork maiden over this trip for her former yard last summer in first-time blinkers; has been well below that level on soft ground since but should do better on this drying surface; blinkers left off; not ruled out. Polar Bear 6 9-3v Mrs J Harrington Darragh O'Sullivan (7) 6-1 59 58 72 On a losing run since April 2023; however, put up a sound effort here over 6f here (sft) on return off this mark; handles better ground so if improving from that has a chance. Step Back In Time 8 9-2p C Timmons Julian Pietropaolo (4) 12-1 58 68 71 All four of her wins have come at this track between 5f-6f, including last October off a 5lb lower mark; not as good next time and tends to need her first run after an absence. An Laochmor 5 9-0b D J Murphy Patrick McGettigan (2) 7-1 56 62 71 Won over this trip on AW at Lingfield and Dundalk the last twice, his only wins; has run well at times on turf including at this course; has to do more but has to be considered. Skillman Ave 4 8-9v J McConnell Jessica O'Gorman (7) 28-1 51 85 73 Sole win came over this trip at Tipperary last July off 68 for Gavin Cromwell and a fine second over 6f here next time; however, has been regressive since and has to get back to form. Andosky 3 8-8t M Mulvany Wesley Joyce 12-1 60 46 75 Best effort when runner-up in a Sligo nursery last year; soundly beaten over 6f and 7f both starts in soft this term; has to improve for better ground and drop in trip. Page 1 spotlightnavan 25.04.26 Apache Star 7 8-8hp1 E Delany Kyle Faulkner (7) 22-1 50 45 73 Three wins when trained in UK with the last in 2023; well beaten in testing ground last twice but might go better today; cheekpieces instead of blinkers. Romantic War 4 8-7b J Murray Freya Frain (7) 50-1 49 34 69 Maiden is out of form and 9lb out of the handicap so look elsewhere.

Though her recent form figures are uninspiring, KILMOOD SUSAN hasn't encountered good ground since winning a Cork maiden last year and is worth taking a chance on at a price. Her stablemate Andosky will appreciate the ground too. Arctic Steps, Sporting Hero, Asdana, Polar Bear and An Laochmor can run well. [Tyrone Molloy] Page 2 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

6f For 2yo only that are EBF eligible Weights 9st 7lbs Penalty value 1st £€12,958 2nd £€4,158 3rd £€1,958 4th £€858 5th £€418 6th £€198 GD-YLD Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR Abletai 2 9-7 M Grassick W J Lee 20-1 - - - First foal; dam 5f winner (RPR 83), half-sister to winners Texas Rock (6f/7f Listed) and We Dare To Dream (7f 2yo/7.4f), out of unraced half-sister to useful 5f/6f 2yo winner Rosabee; dam was useful over this trip and a sibling to some useful sorts; by a quality sire; not ignored. Amigos Legacy 2 9-7 D Hogan Alan Casey (7) 66-1 - - 36 Decent pedigree but was beaten 13l on debut at Dundalk and has to do much better. Arizona Raider 2 9-7 M Mulvany Wesley Joyce (3) 25-1 - 30 69 Not beaten far on recent Curragh debut and can run respectably but likely to find some of these too smart also. Barrow Boy 2 9-7 G Cromwell Gary Carroll 8-1 - - - Fourth foal; half-brother to 7f-1m2f winner for this yard Snellen (inc 2yo/Group 3; RPR 113); dam 1m2f turf/1m4f AW winner (103), half-sister to 1m 2yo Group 3 winner Night Lagoon (dam of King George winner Novellist); by a first-season sire; worth a market check. King Of Cloughan 2 9-7 J P O'Brien J M Sheridan 5-1 - - - Eur110,000 yearling; first foal; dam US 5.5f/6f turf 2yo winner (inc stakes; RPR 99), half-sister to US stakes-placed 1m/8.5f winner Tempers Flair, out of 5.5f stakes winning half-sister to BC Juvenile winner Boston Harbor; by a promising sire; from a quality US damline; a likely player. Tribeca 2 9-7 R De Aguiar Donagh O'Connor 7-4 - - - Eur250,000 yearling was later resold for 575,000gns; second foal; dam 1m2f winner (RPR 80), sister to 1m1f Group 3 winner Carla Bianca, half-sister to 7f Listed winner Joailliere, out of unraced half-sister to 1m4f-1m6f Group 3 winner Profound Beauty; by a leading sire and from a fine Moyglare damline; check the market. West Of Eden 2 9-7 A P O'Brien Ryan Moore 7-4 - - - Second foal; dam 7f 2yo winner (RPR 81), half-sister to 1m4f Listed winner Heliac, out of French 1m5f winning half-sister to winners Meteor Storm (US 1m2f Grade 1) and Polish Summer (UAE 1m4f Group 1); Eur500,000 yearling is by a speed influence with quality stamina in damline; of obvious interest so check the market. Margot Mae 2 9-2 Mrs J Harrington Shane Foley 10-1 - - - A 115,000gns yearling; eighth foal; half-sister to winners incl' New Endeavour (7f-1m1f inc 2yo/AW/Australian Group 3; RPR 117), and Johnny Boom (8.6f-1m4f inc AW; 80); dam unraced half-sister to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Luminous Eyes; by a quality sire and related to lots of winners so check market.

guessing game but Tribeca and WEST OF EDEN look the two of most interest. Both were expensive yearlings and come from yards that have had 2yo winners so far this term. Marginal preference is for the O'Brien-trained runner, but market moves for any of the others would be significant. [Tyrone Molloy] Page 3 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

horses.spotlight_comment: 6f For 3yo only that are EBF eligible Weights 9st 5lbs Penalties Winner of a Group 3 race 3lb extra; of a Group 2 or Group 1 race 5lb extra Penalty value 1st £€29,450 2nd £€9,450 3rd £€4,450 4th £€1,950 5th £€950 6th £€450 GD-YLD Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR Charles Darwin 3 9-10 A P O'Brien Ryan Moore 1-2 110 101 113 Brother to Bluebeard (Prix Morny and Middle Park); only fourth of seven when 4-6 for his Curragh debut (5f, good) last April; made handsome amends with wins in a C&D maiden (soft), a four-runner Naas conditions event (5f good) and the Norfolk Stakes, at the main expense of Middle Park winner Wise Approach; top-class sprinting prospect, reportedly in good shape. Chicago Call 3 9-5 J Murtagh Ben Coen 8-1 100 94 107 Won a 6f Fairyhouse maiden over this trip last July; best form when just denied in a Listed event at the same track in September (6f yielding); below form in the Goffs Million on only 7f attempt; soft ground probably not ideal on seasonal debut at Cork. Frescobaldi 3 9-5 D J Murphy James Ryan 12-1 96 89 102 Ex-Aidan O'Brien won the 7f Convivial at York on his third outing; confirmed a fair standard of form in 7f Listed races at Doncaster and Dundalk before changing hands for 100,000gns; useful prospect for Danny Murphy; unlikely to match former stablemate Charles Darwin. Starman Tom 3 9-5 K Cotter W J Lee 25-1 - 74 93 Showed promise in finishing second behind last season's Queen Mary fourth on debut in a 5f maiden at Cork last month; beaten favourite when third in a big-field 6f maiden of a relatively modest standard at the Curragh last Sunday. Focaccia 3 9-0 J Stack Gavin Ryan 20-1 - 67 76 Debut third at the Curragh four weeks ago suggests she can win races; this looks much too demanding at this stage of her career, but worth a shot with black type available. Kindergarten 3 9-0 Mrs J Harrington Shane Foley 13-2 - 51 97 Made most of the running when a 7/1 winner on debut over C&D last October; placed horses Ocean's Breath and Anushka have both won at Dundalk; should not be out of place at this level. Silk Braid 3 9-0 G Lyons Colin Keane 10-1 - 72 92 Beat a Joseph O'Brien-trained odds-on chance in a 6f Curragh maiden last October on her only start at two; hard to know what level she can reach; tough task against Charles Darwin.

This should be relatively straightforward for the Norfolk Stakes winner CHARLES DARWIN who pleased Aidan O'Brien in a Curragh workout last month. Chicago Call, Listed-placed at two, should be capable of better than he showed at Cork on his seasonal debut and may compete for the place money with Kindergarten, a once-raced maiden winner. [Alan Sweetman] Page 4 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

One of only two horses of Classic age (Stradivarius being the other) to win the Goodwood Cup since 1990, SCANDINAVIA confirmed his high-class staying credentials in the St Leger. In doing so, he reversed Queen's Vase form with the Great Voltigeur winner Carmers who should be suited by drying ground. Emit, who failed to do himself justice on his seasonal debut, is respected on overall form. [Alan Sweetman] Page 5 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

1m6f For 4yo+ Weights 9st 5lbs Penalties (to count from 1st May, 2025 - for races of eleven furlongs or over) Winner of a Group 3 race 3lb extra; of a Group 2 or Group 1 race 5lb extra Penalty value 1st £€30,922.50 2nd £€9,922.50 3rd £€4,672.50 4th £€2,047.50 5th £€997.50 6th £€472.50 GD-YLD Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR Carmers 4 9-10b P Twomey W J Lee 4-1 113 115 118 Won his first three races, notably 1m6f Group 2 Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot, beating the subsequent Geoffrey Freer winner; Furthur; lost his unbeaten record but emerged with credit in taking second in the 1m4f Great Voltigeur at York; hung left and dropped away to finish fifth behind Scandinavia when running on soft for the first time in the St Leger. Scandinavia 4 9-10p A P O'Brien Ryan Moore 4-5 117 119 122 Won four of his five races at three, the exception when a close-up fifth behind Carmers in the 1m6f Queen's Vase; improved with cheekpieces, winning a five-runner 1m5f Group 3 at Newmarket by almost 9l and mastering older stablemate Illinois in the Goodwood Cup (2m, good); dug deep to hold off Rahieb on soft ground in the St Leger (Carmers fifth); top-class stayer. Leinster 5 9-8 J P O'Brien Ronan Whelan 14-1 105 81 115 Stepped outside of handicap company (fourth in Chester Cup and in Ascot Stakes) to win a four-runner St Leger Trial at the Curragh last August, readily brushing aside front-running Dallas Star in the final furlong; faced a very stiff task but ran no sort of race when tailed off in the Irish St Leger. Dallas Star 5 9-5 R De Aguiar Donagh O'Connor 25-1 98 87 114 Won Leopardstown Group 3 in April 2024 (1m2f, heavy); last win was at Dundalk early last year; no match for Leinster in a St Leger trial at the Curragh last August; twice placed in small-field AW events during the winter; well held in third behind Layfayette at the Curragh early this month; up against it. Emit 4 9-5t J P O'Brien J M Sheridan 11-2 111 121 124 Consistent last season apart from a poor run in the Hampton Court Stakes at Royal Ascot. went close in a 1m2f Group 3 at the Curragh in May; Listed winner at Gowran (1m4f, good) in July before runner-up in Group 2 and Group 3 (both over 1m7f on very soft ground) in France; failed to show his best form when fourth behind Layfayette on reappearance at the Curragh. Layfayette 9 9-5p N Meade Colin Keane 10-1 102 94 115 Winner of ten races; last of six stakes race wins was in 2023 Royal Whip over 1m2f at the Curragh; however, he proved that he retains considerable ability and enthusiasm when winning a conditions event over this trip at the Curragh on seasonal debut; (Dallas Star third, Emit fourth), that was his first 1m6f attempt, on his 47th outing. Sunchart 9 9-5 A Slattery Ben Coen 12-1 105 96 115 Useful dual-purpose sort, 3-34 on Flat (and second on ten occasions); his only two stakes race wins from 28 attempts have been in the 1m2f Naas event in which he was third of eight last month; suited by testing conditions, drying ground against him.

One of only two horses of Classic age (Stradivarius being the other) to win the Goodwood Cup since 1990, SCANDINAVIA confirmed his high-class staying credentials in the St Leger. In doing so, he reversed Queen's Vase form with the Great Voltigeur winner Carmers who should be suited by drying ground. Emit, who failed to do himself justice on his seasonal debut, is respected on overall form. [Alan Sweetman] Page 5 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

In theory, Minerva sets the standard with an official rating of 102. Ryan Moore's preference for the less-exposed 92-rated Ice Dancer is significant, but she appears held by THUNDERING ON, based on a Curragh clash last October. Joseph O'Brien's filly has a run under her belt, an advantage she shares with Dundalk maiden winner Emmeleia. [Alan Sweetman] Page 6 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

1m2f For 3yo fillies only Weights 9st 2lbs Penalties (to count from 1st May, 2025) Winner of a Group 3 race 3lb extra; of a Group 2 race or a Group 1 race 5lb extra Penalty value 1st £€41,230 2nd £€13,230 3rd £€6,230 4th £€2,730 5th £€1,330 6th £€630 GD-YLD Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR Bloom 3 9-2 A P O'Brien Ronan Whelan 13-2 - 94 98 Wootton Bassett filly out of a Listed winner by Galileo; stepped up from unplaced debut at Leopardstown to win a 1m maiden at Cork last September; stable's two other runners are more appealing. Camino Vino 3 9-2 G Cromwell Rory Cleary 14-1 - - 89 Invincible Spirit filly created a good impression when beating an 86-rated previous winner in a 1m maiden at Dundalk in December on her only juvenile start; interesting, although not guaranteed to stay as far as this on pedigree. Chasing Paradise 3 9-2 J Murtagh Ben Coen 11-2 - 82 93 Showed promise when 7l second to an experienced Ballydoyle-trained filly over 1m at Leopardstown on sole start at two; stayed this trip well when a winning favourite on soft-to-heavy at the Curragh on reappearance. Emmeleia 3 9-2 D A O'Brien Gavin Ryan 4-1 92 - 98 Half-sister by Camelot to 2025 Lingfield Derby Trial winner Puppet Master; won a 7f barrier trial at Leopardstown last August, second to the promising Yellowstone Lake n a 7f maiden at Dundalk in September; batted well to beat a stablemate over a bit further than this at Dundalk; needs to improve, drying ground should help. Ice Dancer 3 9-2 A P O'Brien Ryan Moore 3-1 92 88 95 Had a troubled run on debut; put that behind her when landing the odds in a 1m maiden at Gowran last September; ground was testing then, and same when she was third in a 1m Group 3 race at the Curragh in October; pedigree implies she can improve at this trip; Ryan Moore prefers her to Minerva who is rated 10lb superior (official and RPR figures). Minerva 3 9-2p A P O'Brien Wayne Lordan 7-2 102 86 105 Ran seven times at two, opening her account on final start, when odds-on in a 7f maiden at Leopardstown; best effort when second to top-class stablemate Diamond Necklace (unbeaten Prix Marcel Boussac winner) in a 7f Curragh conditions event; possible stamina doubt, and Ryan Moore prefers the lower-rated, less exposed Ice Dancer. Thundering On 3 9-2 J P O'Brien J M Sheridan 4-1 - 100 106 Frankel filly, whose dam won the 1m2f Pretty Polly for this stable; fine effort on second juvenile start when second in 1m Group 3 at the Curragh, 4 3/4l in front of third-placed Ice Dancer; touched off in a 1m maiden at Leopardstown 13 days ago; trip will suit, stable in terrific form; could feature here despite her maiden status.

1m2f For 3yo only that are EBF eligible and whose sire established one or more yearling sales in the relevant year with a median price of not more than 50,000euros Weights 9st 8lbs Penalty value 1st £€14,725 2nd £€4,725 3rd £€2,225 4th £€975 5th £€475 6th £€225 GD-YLD Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR African Affair 3 9-8 Ms S Lavery Robbie Colgan 100-1 - - 14 Finished with only one behind him in a 16-runner 7f Naas maiden last autumn; 100-1 shot then; has been gelded. Amethyst Stone 3 9-8 G Lyons James Ryan 25-1 - - - Newcomer is a half-brother to winners in France, Colin Keane rides his 83-rated stablemate. Battle Of Maldon 3 9-8 G Elliott Donagh O'Connor 8-1 - 62 72 Won 7f Naas barrier trial last May; faded in the final furlong of a 7f maiden at Leopardstown the following month; reportedly scoped badly; made an encouraging seasonal debut over 1m at this venue but has a bit to find Huff'N'Puff. Cascade Canyon 3 9-8 K Coleman Julian Pietropaolo (7) 33-1 - 73 74 Showed up well for a long way on debut over C&D; others have much stronger claims. Fay Og 3 9-8 Miss N Lupini Killian Leonard 100-1 - - 20 Huge price when last of 15 at this venue on debut; can be discounted. Genchev 3 9-8 G Lyons Colin Keane 5-1 83 73 90 Made a very encouraging debut when third behind the Aidan O'Brien-trained Daytona in 1m Listed event at Naas last July; but below that level in a Leopardstown maiden later that month on softer ground; faded late into fourth in a 1m1f maiden at Tipperary in August; has been gelded. Glen Echo 3 9-8 G Cromwell Robert Whearty 10-1 - - - Third foal; half-brother to the talented winner Snellen (Chesham Stakes and Group 3 Meld Stakes for this stable); dam 1m2f turf/1m4f AW winner, half-sister to 1m 2yo Group 3 winner Night Lagoon (dam of King George winner Novellist). Good Man Jack 3 9-8 P Magee Wesley Joyce (3) 50-1 - - - Seventh foal; half-brother by Inns Of Court to winners, including multiple scorers Booyea and I Am Not Here; dam Listed-placed 7f winner. Huff'N'Puff 3 9-8 H De Bromhead W J Lee 11-2 - 72 81 Showed promise when keeping on from off the pace in a 1m Curragh maiden last October; confirmed maiden-winning potential with third placing over 1m here on seasonal debut, almost 4l in front of Battle Of Maldon. Kingcharles 3 9-8 K Coleman Rory Cleary 25-1 - - - E38,000 yearling; eighth foal; half-brother to four winners; dam French maiden, out of half-sister to French 2m4f Group 1 winner Karkour. Latin America 3 9-8 J Murtagh Ben Coen 13-8 - 37 100 Gleneagles colt cost 280,000gns as a yearling; unraced at two; chased home possible Irish Derby candidate Shaihaan at the Curragh four weeks ago on debut; form was boosted by his third-placed stablemate Asakir when beating a Joseph O'Brien-trained favourite at Leopardstown. Mergus Serrator 3 9-8 G Cromwell Gary Carroll 16-1 - 68 74 Respectable run at Leopardstown in October on only outing at two; will need to have improved considerably to win this. Now Maybe 3 9-8 Mrs J Harrington Shane Foley 6-1 - 46 87 Struggled on heavy ground first time out at the Listowel festival; looks a possible future winner on his Dundalk second in November. Santa Bravado 3 9-8 A Oliver Ronan Whelan 33-1 - 52 74 Two satisfactory runs last season; likely to be more interesting as a handicap prospect after this. Page 7 spotlightnavan 25.04.26 Youcansaythatagain 3 9-8 A Oliver Gavin Ryan 12-1 - - - 11th foal; half-brother by Ghaiyyath to six winners, notably Dermot Weld-trained Group 2/3 scorer Brooch, and Caponata (Listed) dam, French 5f Listed winner, sister to 1m Group 1 winner Emulous. Croi Gra 3 9-3h Miss N Lupini Wayne Lordan 16-1 - 52 76 Alkumait half-sister to four winners including Holiday Magic (ten wins, all on AW), Coolnagree (two 7f wins, Group 3-placed); respectable debut when third at a big price in a 1m Gowran maiden dominated by market leaders; can improve. Dreamkeeper 3 9-3 N Meade Adam Caffrey 25-1 - - - Fourth foal; half-sister to 6f AW 2yo winner Lady Amanda; dam won twice for Mark Johnston. Teologia 3 9-3 J P O'Brien J M Sheridan 14-1 - 45 77 Dam has produced seven winners, including Rocques (Group 3) and Mea Domina (Listed); showed some ability at Galway last October, but not enough to make her a leading fancy. Tintinabulla 3 9-3h1 Ms S Lavery Siobhan Rutledge (3) 33-1 - - - Fourth foal; half-sister by U S Navy Flag to two minor winners; dam, by Fantastic Light, was a heavily raced AW Listed winner; hooded for debut.

The form of the Curragh maiden in which LATIN AMERICA (nap) finished second is persuasive enough to give him the vote over Genchev who disappointed in maidens after a promising first run in a Listed race. Huff'N'Puff has an edge over Battle Of Maldon on 1m running here. Both have place prospects, along with Now Maybe. [Alan Sweetman] Page 8 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

Tofino 4 9-11 G Cromwell Gary Carroll 12-1 67 50 72 Won a Curragh handicap over 1m last year and some decent runs since between 7f and that trip; up in trip on return and has to prove she stays. Gotta Catch'Em All 6 9-10p H Rogers Adam Caffrey 16-1 66 63 71 Maiden after 22 runs but has been placed several times up to 1m4f; not a bad effort at Leopardstown over 1m on return and should be thereabouts. Pebble Island 4 9-10t J McConnell Donagh O'Connor 20-1 66 65 74 Maiden was beaten a long way over 7f last time at Leopardstown and while he doesn't hold that much appeal can do better over this trip. Wolf Prince 10 9-10 A Melia Gavin Ryan 50-1 66 - 73 Smart hurdler has run well on the Flat in defeat but is returning off a long absence and can only be watched. Faro Island 4 9-9p A Oliver W J Lee 14-1 65 69 73 Won a 1m3f Down Royal handicap last autumn but was poor on AW after (found to have mucus in his lungs); needs best on return but can't be ruled out. Obscenity 4 9-9v1 J P O'Brien J M Sheridan 5-1 65 56 75 Has posted some good runs in defeat since tackling handicaps including on return at Bellewstown over nearly 1m4f; needs more and is unproven in this ground but a player if adapting; visor replaces cheekpieces. Page 9 spotlightnavan 25.04.26 Sonic Invader 4 9-9 N Meade Emily Grifferty (10) 16-1 65 27 65 Not bad runs last two maiden starts of 2025 over 7f and 1m, the latter at this track; has to be ready after a long absence; the market can help. Sylkie 5 9-9p Daniel John Howard Rory Cleary 11-1 65 65 72 Won three handicaps at Galway in 2024; no win last year but some solid efforts up to 1m4f; is fit from hurdling over the winter and can run well. Rain 7 9-8 E & P Harty Jessica O'Gorman (7) 20-1 64 45 69 Won a 1m4f handicap at Galway last year on soft ground but has form on good too; was well beaten on her Curragh return so needs much more. El Regalo 5 9-7 C Murphy Patrick McGettigan (5) 33-1 63 - 73 Dual-purpose maiden was pulled-up over hurdles when last seen; seems best watched back in this sphere after a layoff; new yard. Captain Ciano 4 9-6 T McCourt James Ryan 33-1 62 43 72 Maiden has been poor in two runs on softer ground recently and is not easy to fancy on that form. Casheldale Lass 4 9-6 A Kinirons Robbie Colgan 14-1 62 42 72 Won Gowran and Naas handicaps last year over similar trips to this; not as good last two runs last term and looks vulnerable off this mark. Forlio 7 9-6t P W Flynn Colin Keane 12-1 62 50 73 Won well over C&D last October but wasn't as good off higher marks after and needs more on return down 2lb; eyecatching jockey booking, though. Roman Bull 8 9-1 M O'Meara Wesley Joyce (3) 33-1 57 - 72 Hasn't had much racing in the last two years; is dropping in the weights but still best watched. Searcog 4 8-12t P Magee 54 71 75 First reserve; won a Punchestown handicap last year over 1m1f; some decent hurdle runs over the winter and a solid Leopardstown return over 1m; considered. Frank Pickle 5 10-4 Mrs D Foster 74 60 74 Second reserve; maiden has posted some fine runs in defeat including on return at Curragh (1m); stays 1m4f so can do better over this trip; one to consider. Spanish Rising 4 10-5 H De Bromhead 75 57 67 Third reserve; not bad maiden runs in UK; poor on heavy ground debut for this yard behind a stablemate; can do better now handicapping.

Though she has only run on soft/heavy, it could pay to take a chance that MAEVE BRENNAN will handle this ground and build on her encouraging return. Justenzia is solid and should run well. Pedro The Poet and Sylkie can be players too. Obsenity has a chance but his best form is on softer ground. [Tyrone Molloy] Page 10 spotlightnavan 25.04.26

Juniper Sling 4 10-2 G Lyons Colin Keane 8-1 72 67 73 Half-sister to the talented Thunder Kiss; third in two of her four starts in maidens; ran poorly over 1m2f on heavy ground at Leopardstown on her only handicap start; premature to write off. Trubshaw 4 10-2 H De Bromhead Gabriella Hill (7) 8-1 72 63 73 Two wins last season, both gained at the main expense of members of this field; edged out God The Highness at Sligo; ended the campaign with a 1m6f Curragh victory over Quiz Test; 9lb higher now, same apprentice claiming 7lb. Daboya 5 10-1 R Donohoe Sam Coen (5) 10-1 71 60 72 Versatile mare has won on turf/AW and over hurdles; ground should be coming right for her; lacks the advantage of a recent outing. Granville Street 8 10-0 C Murphy Patrick McGettigan (5) 25-1 70 18 70 Only Flat win came in 2023; fit from hurdling but hard to fancy on recent evidence. Loyal Touch 6 10-0tp D Hogan Julian Pietropaolo (7) 25-1 70 69 74 Five wins for the Johnston yard, but has not shown a great deal in seven AW starts for this stable; down the field at Lingfield early this month. God Of Thunder 7 9-13tp D Hogan Reese Holohan (7) 20-1 69 21 73 Out of form since a Limerick win last June; towards the rear on both turf starts this term. Kool One 5 9-13t C D Maxwell James Ryan 8-1 69 42 72 Won over 1m4f at Roscommon (good) last August and added a Wexford maiden hurdle (good) ten days later; should be better for last month's run when fifth over 1m6f here, 1 3/4l behind the reopposing Earthsong. Radar Ahead 5 9-13 T McCourt Adam Caffrey 20-1 69 48 73 Hurdles winner on good ground; 0-10 on Flat; ran poorly on seasonal debut at Bellewstown; stable appears to have a better chance with Celtic Druid. Goin' 6 9-12 A Martin Harry Sexton (7) 10-1 68 36 73 Twice successful in Germany, suited by 1m4f; struggled over hurdles during the winter; not without a chance on last year's best Flat form, namely a third placing over this trip at Down Royal. Earthsong 4 9-11 W McCreery W J Lee 7-1 67 62 73 Best effort came on handicap debut over1m6f at this venue on yielding ground last August, staying on from the back for a 2l third of 11; should be better for her seasonal debut here last month; has a slight edge with Kool One. Miss Gitana 5 9-11 J Murray Donagh O'Connor 14-1 67 54 72 Three Flat wins, twice in Britain and over 2m at Tramore last April for Gordon Elliott; disappointing over hurdles on last two starts in 2025; makes stable debut. Rich Belief 9 9-11tb K Thornton Robbie Colgan 12-1 67 66 73 Second at Clonmel last September has been the only bright spot since a 2024 Chester win; some merit in his recent Clonmel run. Acheron 5 9-10 J Hanlon Gavin Ryan 20-1 66 - 74 Dam is an unraced half-sister to Irish Derby winner Westover; placed in two of his three Flat starts in France at three; ran creditably in a Dundalk handicap on only start last year; towards the back over 1m2f here last month. Bruant 5 9-10 A Martin Gary Carroll 14-1 66 61 70 Dual-purpose winner has been well beaten last six Flat starts; continues to drop in the handicap; recent Gowran run provides limited encouragement. Page 11 spotlightnavan 25.04.26 Kakori 4 9-10t J P O'Brien J M Sheridan 10-1 66 65 74 Signed off last season with a promising run behind this year's Irish Lincoln winner Ribee at Gowran (7f, heavy); picked up an injury on seasonal debut; also had an excuse at Bellewstown, hampered under half a mile out; not ruled out. Quiz Test 6 9-9 S Byrne Ronan Whelan 8-1 65 70 73 Sole win came at Cork in 2023; decent form in defeat last autumn, including a close third over 1m4f at Galway and second to Trubshaw in a 19-runner contest at the Curragh, with Plunkett Street, Earthsong and Bruant behind; each-way chance if reappearing in similar shape. Plunkett Street 8 9-7 M O'Meara Ben Coen 10-1 63 65 73 Won a 1m4f Cork handicap on return last year and some good runs off higher marks after; won over hurdles in November but disqualified after a positive sample; failed to run to market expectations at Gowran on seasonal debut, capable of better. Celtic Druid 5 9-6 T McCourt Sadhbh Tormey (7) 13-2 62 44 72 Progressive in winning back-to-back 1m4f handicaps at Dundalk; appeared to have plenty left in the tank last time; those two runs, if not his pedigree, suggest the extra two furlongs will be within his range; holds a leading chance here with Sadhbh Tormey's claim in play again. God The Highness 4 9-5 Mrs J Harrington Shane Foley 10-1 61 49 74 Chance here with fitness advanced by a hurdles run at Fairyhouse; went close against Trubshaw in a small-field Sligo event last August; probably a better effort third of 23 over 1m6f here in October. Arcland 10 8-12 G Cromwell Robert Whearty 54 56 71 First reserve; went very close in a similar race here on his penultimate Flat start last year; went on to win over hurdles before a below-par Bellewstown run; durable sort. Edge Of Darkness 6 8-7tp Daniel John Howard Rory Cleary 49 - 73 Second reserve; a four-time turf winner whose recent Dundalk form has been poor. Timeless Charm 5 10-3 R De Aguiar 73 63 73 Third reserve; both wins in Britain came on AW; drying ground should help for Irish debut.

With race-fitness on his side and drying conditions a plus factor, CELTIC DRUID can maintain the progress evident at Dundalk. Quiz Test and Trubshaw renew a late-season Curragh rivalry that suggests they can feature. Earthsong and Kool One are closely matched on last month's clash at this venue and should enter calculations. [Alan Sweetman] Page 12
